podcast.title: Manager of U2
podcast.body: Paul McGinnis became the manager of U2 after receiving a recommendation from Barry Devlin, bassist and vocalist of Horslips, who knew McGinnis was a big fan of Horslips. "And that's how Paul McGinnis became the manager of U2."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: U2 Manager
podcast.body: Paul McGuinness served as the manager for U2. He recognized the exceptional skills of local roadie Greg Carroll during U2's 1984 tour and subsequently hired Carroll for the remainder of the tour. "U2 manager Paul McGinnis hired Greg to be with U2 for the remainder of the tour."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

xref.title: First Client of Paul McGuinness
xref.body: Sean Davy was Paul McGuinness's first client in band management. Davy achieved a hit song that originated from a TV commercial for the National Dairy Council, titled "Waitvert, The Pride of the Horde."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Local Roadie for U2
xref.body: Greg Carroll was a local roadie from Auckland, New Zealand, initially hired by U2 to assist with production during their "Unforgettable Fire" tour in Australia and New Zealand in 1984. His exceptional performance led U2 manager Paul McGuinness to hire him for the remainder of the tour. "He was a local Rody hired to help out with their production."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

xref.title: Managerial Learning for Paul McGuinness
xref.body: Irish folk rock band Horslips were quite successful in Ireland, and their manager was a friend of Paul McGuinness. By "hanging around with them," McGuinness gained valuable insights and learned several aspects of being a manager, which later informed his own career.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
